notes.title: Patch 1.5.0
notes.content:
[h2]Sprite Sheet maker[/h2]
For a long time I was continously meeting with the same issue: I can't decent sprite sheet maker for frame by frame animation that would be fast (which instantly removes Gimp and Photoshop plugins), would be without obvious bugs, would allow for realtime result preview and would be free. 

So best course of action was to make my own. Decision was made to simply integrate it into ModLab. With ModLab 1.5 I am releasing this feature to public. Here you can see short video presenting some of possiblities (it was made in middle of the development, some things changed, some were polished).

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y1GvjsC0TqQ

[h2]Batch Exporter[/h2]
There are two other features that were requested. The first one is batch exporter, in this iteration, it is very basic and won't support more complex functionality like combine normal maps, however, it will work fine for basic Normal from Diffuse/Height. It exports normal and roughness map, usage should be extremely simple as can be seen in this gif:

[img]https://media3.giphy.com/media/Hpf200DIuasGPOD6j0/giphy.gif[/img]

[h2]Reflectance Map[/h2]
Another feature is relevant only for the Wayward Terran Frontier modding community. Modlab now supports Reflectance map preview (as used by the game's engine). In the future I would like to include the rest of PBR including metalness and offer preview mode for Wayward Terran Frontier or general PBR usage (as I use one in my own engine).

[img]https://media1.giphy.com/media/dPTKkLgSFUloQUCwDY/giphy.gif[/img]

One more minor feature was implemented as requested, which is clamping normal map according to alpha:

To use it, simply check "Alpha Clip Normal" under Diffuse menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31777225/4d860966e70d4978a3b48f15e6a2cb712af2fb8f.png[/img]

While this version was used in production it can always use more testing, if you come across some issue please let me know, I will try to release fix as soon as possible.

If you would like to support this project, as well as my other projects, please considering visiting my Patreon page: https://www.patreon.com/RavensLab

notes.title: Patch 1.3.0
notes.content:
This patch was focused around Nebula generator. This is first working interation of said feature that will let you export backgrounds into PNG. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31777225/49367b14fc88f49c928ab3cbf205fb4385fc9139.png[/img]

Video tutorial will be up in few days, but in meantime there are some instructions:

[list]
[*] After starting ModLab click "Background" on top bar. 
[*] Now you can start loading assets into Level 0. 
[*] If you don't have assets or if you want to use default assets, you can click "Load Base assets" in bottom left menu to load 5 normal maps.
[*] From this point on, it should be straight forward: Poke sliders till you like the result. 
[*] You can use left click to move omni lights, right click to open their content menu, espace to close that menu.
[*] Exported PNGs includes alpha channel, you can remove it in any 2D editor if you don't want to that channel. You are not losing anything because of existence of said data and when removed you will get the exact result you seen before export. You can however use it to create multiple layers and such.
[/list]

Next Patron poll will including features extending background generator as well as normal map related feature. We will see what community will pick.

As of the moment there might be some rough edges. If you encounter some fatal issue then please let me know. If you would like to support development of this app check Patreon https://www.patreon.com/user?u=7785848

Big thanks to all current Patrons.

notes.title: Patch 1.2 and Tutorial video
notes.content:
Second Patreon voting poll concluded some time ago and I bring goodies. Results shown that users want to improve roughness map, which was admittedly
the weakest part of ModLab. To improve it I need some extra data, specifically curvature. This version of ModLab let you generate curvature from Normal map and use it to improve Roughness map. On top of it even if you provide your own Roughness map you can use new data to add some details to it.

As seen here:
[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/4QFL474mkqMLFiXbWJ/giphy.gif[/img]

Curvature itself is quite powerful information. For that reason if Curvature is generated it will get saved (unless exporting for WTF:ZF format) and can be used in any 2D editors. Red channel contains grey mid point information, green isolated edges and blue isolated cavities.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/mPIvPvbDuRtYJfKHCp/giphy.gif[/img]

I made quick tutorial about using ModLab for sprite:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9lKMgj9lwKw

Change log:
-New Roughness processing!
-Large amount of features relevant to roughness
-Curvature from Normal map
-Wrote bypass for PNG compression
-Rare bug when part of saved image is missing should be fixed
-Better GUI separators

notes.title: Preview: patch v1.1 part 2
notes.content:
Alright, so other part of this update: Optimization
 
First of all I need a reasonable goal. Processing a 4k x 4k texture on a 4 years old mid tier GPU at 60 fps seems like a reasonable goal, so let's aim for that. To make it fun let's include the latest changes with the most performance hungry settings (using largest possible kernels for small and medium elements).
 
So initial test: Load texture, Generate From Diffuse set, set the highest radius for both elements + using most complicated kernel aaaaand we are at 17 fps. Alright, so I need to make this aprox 3 times faster. In terms of rendering this is kinda scary especially considering that I was trying to make this efficient in first place and I am not going to compromise quality in any way.
 
First of all let's do some profiling to see what's the most expensive, I have pretty good idea but it is good to confirm and see how exactly expensive it is. What we have learned at this point is that VS graphic debugging sucks. The moment I am under 60 fps (thus the point you want to profile) I am unable to capture a frame and the whole debugging process glitches. Well it's not like I am mad, I am just furious. Ok then, let's profile smaller texture and just use the ratios between individual processing steps. Okay, so I can now capture a frame, I can get quick analysis but I can't get extended "Error have occured" - Thx for info, I almost didn't notice. *flips table* Alright , let's roll with Nsight. Luckily for me Nsight works like a charm. Profiling confirmed what I expected. While at it I've noticed minor Color Surfaces mismatch and here we have another fps. In other words 53 ms per frame, I would need to get to aprox 16.7 ms for frame to be at 60 fps. Currently worst offenders are processing added recently and for those there is no possible optimization as they are simply blurs with large kernel (remember when I said that I wont compromise quality, so no, I am not going to undersample these, blurs shaders used here already make advantage of linear interpolation). The most reasonable way at this point is to process these only when required, thus on value change, it is obvious approach, really which I was avoiding for few minor reasons but I guess it's time. TL DR version of what's going to happen: There are several parallel processing branches running at same time, some are merging at some points, all are contributing to final result. Goal here is to update minimum portion of the "tree" system when their input changes. After these changes we are suddenly at 46-47 fps with very minor fps drop (3-4fps) when moving sliders, everything still responds in realtime, 13fps/5ms to go. So let's give same treatment to billateral processing.

[url=https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31777225/01160601c1c84ff54ac31b79d076c49f3b5a17e1.png][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31777225/65cb0842f7d782ae2680dcd26b18763c0e9bc7fc.png[/img][/url]
 
Changes above resulted in improvement from 17 to 56 fps with worst case scenario drop to 49 fps for split second (realistically unnoticeable). I've tested also some 8k x 2.5k textures and performance was still very reasonable. This concludes optimization pass for patch 1.1. Main feature still remain changes regarding large and medium elements as mentioned in previous post: https://steamcommunity.com/games/768970/announcements/detail/1671276544921786698
 
So when is v1.1 going to be released? Probably during next week, no promises there, I want to clean up few things, finish slider value normalization and add few other QoL improvements (scroll wheel to scroll left side of GUI incoming).
 
As always I would like to thanks all Patrons, you are the reason why I am working on this patch.
 
Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/user?u=7785848

notes.title: Preview: patch v1.1
notes.content:
[b]First Patreon[/b] poll concluded some time ago and since then I am have been working on the two most voted options. Since talking about optimization would be boring I will talk about other one, which is nothing else than quality of medium and large generated elements.
 
[h1]The issue:[/h1]
As I stated in the poll I knew about the issue. I generally discouraged people from using medium and large elements and stick with pixel perfect small ones which would do for most of the cases but not always and it was limiting factor for Modlab's flexibility.
 
The issue was caused by my approach for medium and large elements which was to simply undersample input data thus processing smaller images and then upscaling them back.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31777225/87d0487bd881cac1b7db79f4047c2644ffd1b664.png[/img]

As you can see on the images above that caused some artifacts and that wont do.

[h1]The solution:[/h1]
To greatly improve quality I changed how processing of mentioned elements works. Instead of simply undersampling, input data are processed by filtering and since all processing in ModLab is so far realtime it provides decent options. Not only that artifacts were removed and quality greatly increased, but new options are now available. You can now chose radius of medium and large elements as well as Z profile of processing filter giving you even more control over results.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/1ykANmMsAANHW5unZE/giphy.gif[/img]
 
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31777225/b2fa1b5c310106e465ef1a948f85f0d87f6b99a2.png[/img]

[h1]What's next:[/h1]
I will now spend some more time working on other most voted option, which is optimizations. I have some plans on that matter but don't expect miracles. Generating and processing normal maps in realtime simply aren't cheapest operations. Once everything is ready I will release v1.1 patch. There is chance I will release some tutorial videos or at very least I will be streaming how I use upcoming version of ModLab to process some sprite assets stream will be later on available on Youtube and linked here.
 
[h1]Special thanks:[/h1]
I would like to thank Patrons, for your financial support and your help in deciding direction of ModLab development.
